results.title: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi ship, govt-held areas
results.description: Sanaa, Aug 12 (IANS) Yemen's Houthi group has confirmed that it had targeted what it described as a Saudi military equipment transport ship in the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, as well as Saudi-backed forces in the government-held areas of Mocha and Marib. In a statement posted on social media platform X on Tuesday (local time), the Houthis' military media centre said the group's forces had carried out an operation targeting "a Saudi military equipment transport ship" in Bab al-Mandab. It did not identify the vessel or provide further details about the operation. In a separate statement on X, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said "a large number of ballistic missiles and drones" targeted troop gatherings, weapons depots and command centres in Mocha, a coastal city in southwestern Taiz province, and at Tadawin military camp in the northeastern province of Marib. Sarea claimed the strikes were "precise" and caused dozens of casualties, including Saudi personnel. There was no immediate confirmation of the claimed casualties from Saudi Arabia or the Yemeni government, reports Xinhua news agency. Meanwhile, pro-government Coast Guard troops said in an updated statement that the commercial vessel Tihamah came under repeated missile attacks while sailing through Bab al-Mandab earlier Tuesday, leaving six people dead and 10 others wounded. Four of the dead were crew members -- three Pakistanis and one Indonesian -- while the other two were members of the pro-government 2nd Naval Forces Brigade, according to the statement. The statement said seven other crew members, two Coast Guard personnel and one member of the 2nd Naval Forces Brigade were wounded and are receiving medical treatment. The Coast Guard said its troops, working with rescue teams from government forces, evacuated the casualties after the strikes sparked a fire aboard the vessel and caused significant damage. The Bab al-Mandab Strait, which connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden, is one of the world's key maritime chokepoints and a vital route for international trade and energy shipments. --IANS sd/

results.title: CISF detects skull concealed in passenger’s hand baggage at Delhi airport
results.description: New Delhi, Aug 12 (IANS) Alert personnel of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) deployed at Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport, New Delhi, detected a skull concealed inside a passenger’s hand baggage during a pre-embarkation security check on Wednesday. The passenger was scheduled to travel from Delhi to Hyderabad. During the security screening process, CISF personnel noticed a suspicious object hidden inside the passenger’s hand baggage. Upon questioning, the passenger claimed that the recovered item was a monkey skull. Given the nature of the object and its suspected link to wildlife, the passenger was handed over to the local police for further legal action under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The incident underscores the alertness and vigilance of CISF personnel in ensuring aviation security and their proactive role in supporting the enforcement of laws aimed at protecting wildlife and preventing the illegal transport of wildlife-related items. Earlier, on January 24, panic briefly erupted at Terminal 3 of Delhi’s IGI Airport after a box containing what appeared to be a human skeleton was discovered within the airport premises. The finding triggered a security alert, prompting Delhi Police and other security agencies to rush to the spot and conduct thorough checks. However, subsequent investigations revealed that the skeleton was not real but a model commonly used in medical colleges for educational purposes. According to Delhi Police, the box was found in the departure area near an airline office between 9 a.m. and 10 a.m. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Airport) Vichitra Veer had said, “During inquiry, it emerged that a passenger had left the box with airline staff after being denied permission to carry it on the flight. The item was later noticed by housekeeping staff, who alerted DIAL security, which in turn informed the local police.” Police officials had stated that no suspicious material was found and that the situation was handled in accordance with established security protocols. However, to ensure complete compliance with all procedures, the skeleton was sent for forensic examination. --IANS jk/dpb

results.title: Two dead, several feared trapped after landslide in Mumbai's Ghatkopar; rescue operation on
results.description: Mumbai, Aug 12 (IANS) At least two people died and four to five others were feared trapped after a landslide struck a chawl in Mumbai’s Ghatkopar area in the early hours of Wednesday, officials said. Rescue and relief operations are underway, with multiple agencies engaged to locate and evacuate those trapped beneath the debris. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) and the Mumbai Fire Brigade, the incident occurred at around 3:48 a.m. at Gaushiya Chawl in Chirag Nagar, Ghatkopar. Preliminary reports indicate that a portion of a hillock collapsed onto the chawl, causing debris to fall on two to three houses. Authorities initially feared that five to six people had been trapped in the incident. Following the landslide, Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde and Additional Municipal Commissioner (Eastern Suburbs) Dr. Avinash Dhakne visited the affected site to assess the situation and monitor the ongoing rescue efforts. Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Ganesh Shinde confirmed that two people lost their lives in the incident, while several others are still believed to be trapped under the debris. Speaking to reporters, Shinde said, “Rescue operations are underway, with emergency response teams and local authorities continuing their efforts at the site. While we cannot confirm the exact number at this stage, it is suspected that three to four people may still be trapped beneath the debris.” He added that the bodies of the deceased have been sent to a hospital for further procedures. “The Ghatkopar Police will take the necessary legal action and conduct a detailed investigation into the incident,” he said. Rescue operations are being carried out jointly by personnel from the Mumbai Fire Brigade, Mumbai Police, and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF). Two injured persons have been admitted to hospital. They were identified as 18-year-old Sohel Ansari, who suffered a head injury, and 14-year-old Mohamad Ansari, who sustained a back injury. Both are reported to be in stable condition. Authorities continue to clear debris and search for survivors. Further details are awaited. --IANS jk/dpb

results.title: Aditi Malikk reacts to pregnancy rumours after being trolled for her weight: It’s a mother’s body, I don’t take shortcuts
results.description: Mumbai, August 12 (IANS) Actress and television personality Aditi Malikk has spoken out about the ‘ugly’ comments she recently received about her body after she posted a video featuring herself on her social media account. She urged people to be more considerate before passing judgements on someone’s appearance. The actress opened up after a recent social media post led several people to assume that she was pregnant simply because her paunch was visible in the way she was sitting. Taking to her social media account, Aditi shared a video addressing the comments and said that remarks about weight, bloating or someone’s stomach may seem harmless to the person making them but can have a much deeper impact on the person receiving them. “You put on weight, you have a lot of weight on your stomach, oh your face looks bloated,” she said, urging people to be more mindful before commenting on someone’s appearance. “I feel everyone should be a little more considerate when they comment, whether it's in person or on social media,” Aditi said. The actress then spoke about a post she had shared a few days earlier, which prompted pregnancy assumptions because of the way she was sitting. “2-3 days ago, I posted a post where people thought I was pregnant. Because the way I was sitting, I could see my paunch my stomach,” she said. Aditi made it clear that she is comfortable with her body and does not allow such comments to dictate how she sees herself. “I honestly am not very conscious about all this because I love my body, I respect my body, it's a mother's body,” she said. “I personally believe that being healthy is more important.” “So I don't take any shortcuts,” Aditi said, adding that managing one’s health can become challenging when daily responsibilities and food habits are taken into consideration. Towards the end of the video, she said, “Comments matter a lot. Whatever we comment about, we don't know when that thing hurts someone.” “I think we all should understand that. Good day,” she concluded. Alongside the video, Aditi also shared a message asking people to pause before making assumptions about others. She wrote, “Not everything you see on social media needs a comment, a question or an assumption. There’s always more to someone’s life than what makes it to the feed. So, before we hit “send”, maybe pause and think, would I say this if they were standing right in front of me? A little more thought before we comment, a little less assumption and a little more kindness wouldn’t hurt.” For the uninitiated, Aditi, who is married to actor Mohit Maalikk, embraced motherhood when the couple welcomed their son Ekbir in 2021. On the professional front, known for her television work, Aditi has been associated with shows including Shararat, Banoo Main Teri Dulhann, Meri Awaaz Ko Mil Gayi Roshni, Pyaar Ko Ho Jaane Do and Kumkum Bhagya, apart from appearing in other television projects. –IANS rd/
